acceptedAnswer.text: UGC means user-generated content. In advertising it usually means creator-style video with real people talking about a product, made to run as paid ads.
We brief creators to fit your product and audience, and direct the shoot against the brand thesis.

mainEntity.name: How much creative do you make?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your ad spend and your testing plan, and we agree it after the audit call.

mainEntity.name: Do you make creative for B2B and education too?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Creative is part of the lead generation work we do for B2B and education brands, as video, statics and landing-page content.

mainEntity.name: How do you know which videos work?

acceptedAnswer.text: We test versions against each other and read hook rate, hold rate and cost per result together with your media buying.
It depends on scope and, for media, on ad spend, so we quote after the audit call, once we have seen your accounts.

points.title: One brand thesis
points.text: Every video is briefed against a single idea, so tests have a direction.

points.title: Creators, not stock
points.text: Real people talking about the product in a natural way.

points.title: A steady refresh
points.text: New versions arrive on a schedule, before results tire.

leaks.lede: Creative is one of the biggest levers in paid media and one of the first to tire. Each stage below is where it goes wrong, and how we run it.

stages.breaks: Making videos with no shared idea behind them.
stages.why: Random creative cannot be compared, so nothing is learned. A clear idea gives every new video a reason.
stages.does: We write a brand thesis and short briefs for each video, so every test asks a clear question.

stages.breaks: Polished ads that look like ads.
stages.why: Feeds tend to reward content that looks like it belongs there. Creator-style video often earns more attention than a studio spot.
stages.does: We brief and shoot creator-style videos with real people, on location or at home, matched to your audience.

stages.why: The first seconds decide whether anyone keeps watching, and each platform and placement has its own shape.
stages.does: We edit each video with strong hooks and cut versions for the formats and placements you run.

stages.why: The videos a team likes are not always the ones an audience watches. Only results show which ones hold attention.
stages.does: We test versions against each other and read the results together with your media buying, so the next round builds on what worked.

stages.breaks: Running the same creative until it stops working.
stages.why: Every ad tires. A steady supply of new versions keeps results from falling off suddenly.
stages.does: We plan a steady flow of new versions, so fresh creative is ready before the current set tires.
